question: If L is the mid-point of side BC of ΔABC and the area of ΔABL is 15 cm², then the area (in sq cm) of ΔABC is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any triangle, the **median** (the line joining a vertex to the **mid-point** of the opposite side) bisects the **area** of the triangle into two equal parts.

Since **L** is the **mid-point** of **BC**, **AL** is the **median** of **ΔABC**.

∴ Area of **ΔABC** = 2 × Area of **ΔABL**

⇒ Area of **ΔABC** = 2 × 15 = 30 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Area of **ΔABL** = 15 cm² and **L** is the **mid-point** of side **BC**.

**Formula Used:** Area of a triangle = (1/2) × base × height. Triangles with the same height have areas proportional to their bases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2bf57797a61deb7c222fde96a7662aedd9516725dcca31f7c0ac4c8f8b0704c3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Both **ΔABL** and **ΔALC** share the same altitude from vertex **A** to the line **BC**.

⇒ Area(ΔABL) / Area(ΔALC) = Base(BL) / Base(LC)

⇒ Since **L** is the **mid-point**, BL = LC, which means Base(BL) / Base(LC) = 1.

⇒ Area(ΔALC) = Area(ΔABL) = 15 cm²

⇒ Area(ΔABC) = Area(ΔABL) + Area(ΔALC)

⇒ Area(ΔABC) = 15 + 15 = 30 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 30 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Centroid Property

The three medians of a triangle intersect at the **centroid**, dividing the triangle into 6 smaller triangles of equal area.

Area and Base Ratio

If a point D divides the base BC in the ratio m:n, then Area(ΔABD) : Area(ΔADC) = m : n.

Apollonius Theorem

In ΔABC with median AL, the sum of the squares of two sides is: AB² + AC² = 2(AL² + BL²).</p
